description: Maps a change in the governed production surface to the Pine modules, trace fields, golden fixtures and parity stages it invalidates. Consumed by tools/oracle/impact.py. Every 'production' path is a real file in the 30-file governed manifest (live/engine_manifest.json) or in the live wrapper; every 'stage' is a stage in the Phase 0 audit section 18.

categories.NO_ORACLE_IMPACT: The changed surface is not mirrored by Pine. Record and move on.
categories.CONFIG_ONLY_ORACLE_UPDATE: Algorithms unchanged; regenerate config constants and re-run affected fixtures.
categories.GENERATED_CONSTANTS_UPDATE: An enum, reason code or lookup table changed. Regenerate; generation FAILS if Pine has no mapping.
categories.ALGORITHM_PARITY_UPDATE: A decision rule changed. The named Pine module must be re-derived from the new Python and its fixtures re-baselined.
categories.TRACE_SCHEMA_UPDATE: The per-bar trace shape changed. Bump trace_schema_version and regenerate every fixture.
categories.PINE_LIMITATION_CHANGE: The feasibility of mirroring something changed. The limitation register must be reviewed.
categories.FULL_PARITY_REVALIDATION_REQUIRED: Change is broad or crosses several subsystems. Re-run every stage.

default_for_unmapped_governed_file.rationale: Fail closed. A governed file with no entry here is one nobody has classified, so it must not be assumed harmless. Add an explicit entry instead of widening this default.

entries.surface: the 120-field config dataclass the Golden JSON overrides
entries.notes: A DEFAULT changes only what the Golden JSON does not override, so most edits here are inert. The extractor still fails closed: extract_contract exits 3 if a field listed in PINE_RELEVANT_CONFIG disappears, and exits 4 if a default flips an UNSUPPORTED_IF_ACTIVE flag.

entries.surface: cohort rule compilation, eligibility base/rescue/block, state target overrides
entries.notes: 164 populated cells today (24 cohorts + 78 state-override + 62 eligibility-state). Never hand-transcribe.

entries.surface: spread/slippage/commission applied to every row
entries.notes: Config constants, not live spread.

entries.surface: M1 to 15m aggregation
entries.notes: Empty intervals are DROPPED by dropna, so bar_index is not a uniform time grid (limitation L-09).

entries.surface: report/validator/shim modules not reached by execute_scenario_job
entries.notes: Governed (so they move engine_manifest_id and therefore the fingerprint) but NOT on the live decision path. A change here makes the oracle STALE_ENGINE without making it wrong — re-stamp the manifest, no fixture rerun needed. strategy_core/ghost_tracker.py is inert under the deployed config.

entries.surface: Lux's own 3-file digest, gated at startup
entries.notes: Changes the fingerprint (so the build reads STALE_ENGINE) without changing any rendered decision. Re-stamp the manifest; no fixture rerun.

entries.surface: entry / stop / target / risk computation
entries.notes: risk <= 0 silently rejects the candidate with no trade row (blocking matrix B01).

entries.surface: 25% wick arm, +3 candle delay, in-range fill gate
entries.notes: The compound fill gate is one expression at execution.py:2644; treat any edit to that line as an algorithm change.

entries.surface: stop/target resolution incl. the fill-candle special case
entries.notes: Stop wins same-candle ambiguity; a same-candle TP needs gap-fill or a confirming close.

entries.surface: far-edge invalidation (execution.py:2957-2968)
entries.notes: No dedicated Python test exists for this rule — Phase 0 flagged it as a coverage gap. Add a fixture before relying on it.

entries.surface: re-export shims and the package surface
entries.notes: src/order_blocks.py re-exports strategy_core.order_blocks; strategy_core/__init__.py is the public surface; strategy_core/swings.py::detect_swings is DEAD on the live path (the live pipeline uses the inlined loop inside detect_order_blocks). A change to any of these moves engine_manifest_id but cannot change a rendered decision. CAUTION: if __init__.py ever stops re-exporting a symbol the extractor imports, extraction fails loudly rather than silently — that is intended.

entries.surface: 15m boundary arithmetic and the frozen/live seam
entries.notes: Drives the INTRA-WINDOW marking in S12.

entries.surface: frame diff to broker intents
entries.notes: Only SKIP_INTRA_WINDOW is Pine-reproducible; the rest is execution state Pine cannot see (limitations L-12..L-15).

entries.surface: hard rails and reconciliation
entries.notes: Pine has no broker, ledger or account state. Recorded so the HUD banner text stays honest, but no fixture depends on it.

entries.surface: daily EMA/BBW/ADX panel and the 6-state classifier
entries.notes: UTC calendar days, shifted one day (limitation L-06). Eligibility is keyed on marketState, so any change here also invalidates S10.

entries.surface: blackout and flatten window matching
entries.notes: Unreproducible in Pine (limitation L-07). A change here alters how many rows must be EXCLUDED from parity scoring, so the limitation register and the exclusion counts must be reviewed.

entries.surface: driver-side OB status vocabulary used by the chart layer
entries.notes: This vocabulary does NOT cover STATE_BLOCKED / COHORT_DISABLED / REGIME_BLOCKED — they fall through to 'unknown' (809 of 2080 OBs in the committed golden run). The oracle extends it deliberately; see oracle_status_extensions in the contract.

entries.surface: hand-written Pine fragments assembled into the generated artefact
entries.notes: Editing a fragment REQUIRES regeneration: check_freshness compares fragment hashes against the manifest and reports STALE_CONTRACT until `generate_pine --write` is re-run. The assembled file itself must never be hand-edited (reported INCOMPATIBLE).

entries.surface: the oracle's transparent replay of the S2/S3/S4 production algorithms
entries.notes: This is the REFERENCE the Pine fragments mirror, so an edit here changes every S2-S4 trace. selfcheck() replays a real frame and asserts the order blocks it WOULD produce match detect_order_blocks field for field (verified: 350/350 over 2 years). If that check fails the replay has drifted and the trace is lying.

entries.surface: OB bounds, origin selection tie-break, size gate, ob_id counter
entries.notes: ob_id is history-start dependent (limitation L-05); fixtures match on (detection_time, direction, top, bottom), never on id.

entries.surface: volatility measure and the parsed_high/parsed_low flip
entries.notes: First-value-seeded RMA. ta.rma/ta.atr are SMA-seeded and measured to agree on 0 of 1818 bars (max 27.4% rel). Parsed prices feed the S5 order-block BOX only — NOT swings or breaks, which read raw prices. An S2 divergence therefore cannot move a swing or a BOS.

entries.surface: deployed decision table and the enforce-mode gate
entries.notes: Pine must encode the EFFECTIVE table (post with_disabled_as_label), not the deployed one.

entries.surface: UTC hour-of-day session table
entries.notes: Session keys feed the cohort gate, so a session change is also a cohort change.

entries.surface: BOS/CHoCH break detection + swing_trend_bias (order_blocks.py:173-220)
entries.notes: Two-bar RAW CLOSE test with asymmetric operators (prev<=lvl & cur>lvl for bulls). Bull is evaluated FIRST and both blocks can fire on one bar. swing_trend_bias is NEVER reset and is seeded by the first break in LOADED history — limitation L-04, the correctness cliff.

entries.surface: inlined swing-leg loop (order_blocks.py:144-171)
entries.notes: strategy_core/swings.py::detect_swings is DEAD on the live path; changing it alone has NO oracle impact. Only the loop INLINED in detect_order_blocks matters. It reads RAW high/low, uses STRICT comparisons, records only on a leg TRANSITION, and retains one uncrossed swing per side.

entries.surface: UTC calendar-day key used for the regime panel lookup
entries.notes: Shared with S6: the regime panel keys on this day. Pine must derive it from the bar timestamp — request.security(...,'D',...) follows the EXCHANGE session day and is rejected by tools/oracle/lint_pine.py.

stage_dependencies._note: A failure or change at a stage invalidates every stage that consumes it. S1 defines the bar series everything else is computed on; S3's swings are what S4 breaks; S2's parsed prices set the S5 order-block box. Enforced by tools/oracle/compare_stages.py.
